passage: I am Vaibhav, and I was in the shop when I saw two toddlers by the toy shelf. Indu, about two, grabbed a red car out of another child's hands. He wailed. Her father knelt and said gently, "Say sorry, Indu." She muttered, "Sorry," and pushed the car back into the boy's hand, then patted his arm. I doubt she knew she had done wrong, but her hand was gentle.

qa.q: What did Indu take from the other child?
qa.a: She grabbed a red car.

qa.q: What does Indu's gentle pat after returning the car suggest, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: It suggests she wanted to make things better after her father's prompt. She may only have been copying, without understanding that she had upset the boy.

qa.q: What could Indu's father do next to help her learn?
qa.a: He can keep showing simple repair, like giving the toy back and offering a hug, and say the boy felt sad without heavy blame.

qa.q: How might the boy feel when Indu pats him?
qa.a: He may feel comforted to have his car back, but he might still feel upset for a while.

grounding: A toddler who grabbed a toy hands it back and gives a gentle gesture after a prompted sorry, showing early reparation.

passage: On Monday Tanvir, two, snatched a truck from his cousin. Sudha said, "Tanvir, sorry?" and he handed it back, looking at the floor. On Wednesday he grabbed a spoon from his cousin and, when she cried, gave it back and flung his arms round her, without any prompt. On Friday he took her cup again and only gave it back when Sudha reminded him. Sudha thought the giving back was growing, though the grabbing was not gone yet.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do on Wednesday when his cousin cried?
qa.a: He gave back the spoon and hugged her without being told.

qa.q: What might Tanvir have felt when he handed back the truck on Monday, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: He may have felt uneasy because Sudha's tone changed and his cousin was upset. He may also just have been following her instruction, without seeing his own fault.

qa.q: What could Sudha do to support Tanvir's progress?
qa.a: Sudha can keep prompting simply, notice warmly when he repairs, and not expect him to stop grabbing all at once. 🙂

qa.q: How might Tanvir's cousin experience these three days?
qa.a: She probably feels upset when things are taken, but the hug and returned toys tell her he cares.

grounding: A toddler offers a toy back or a hug after prompting, showing early reparation rather than understanding of fault.

passage:
In the playground of their Bengaluru apartment block, Thomas grabbed Ramesh's toy truck and ran off. Ramesh sat down and wailed.
Thomas's mother knelt beside him. "Ramesh is crying. He was playing with that. Can you give it back and say sorry?"
Thomas stared at Ramesh. Then he walked over, held out the truck, and gave him a clumsy hug round the neck. Ramesh stopped crying and took the truck.

qa.q: What did Thomas grab from Ramesh?
qa.a: Ramesh's toy truck.

qa.q: What might Thomas have been feeling when he stared at Ramesh?
qa.a: He may have been puzzled or a little uneasy seeing Ramesh cry, without fully understanding it was his fault.

qa.q: What did Thomas's mother do that helped repair the moment?
qa.a: She explained simply what happened and prompted him to give the truck back and say sorry.

qa.q: How might Ramesh feel about the clumsy hug?
qa.a: Ramesh probably felt comforted and less upset once he had the truck and the hug.

grounding: A toddler gives back a grabbed toy and hugs after a prompt, an early act of repair rather than understanding fault.

passage:
"Ira, Mehak is crying. You took her crayon."
Ira clutched the purple crayon and looked at her cousin.
"Can you give it back?" asked Ira's mother. "And say sorry."
Ira held the crayon out. Mehak took it, sniffing.
"Sorry?" prompted her mother.
"Sowwy," said Ira, and patted Mehak's head twice.
Mehak giggled through her tears. "Okay, Ira."

qa.q: What colour was the crayon?
qa.a: Purple.

qa.q: What might Ira have been feeling as she clutched the crayon?
qa.a: She wanted the crayon and may have felt unsure about giving it back, though Mehak's crying seemed to make her uneasy.

qa.q: Why does the prompted "sorry" still matter at Ira's age?
qa.a: Because giving back and patting shows her how to repair, even before she understands fault.

qa.q: How does Mehak react to the pat on her head?
qa.a: Mehak giggles through her tears, feeling better and forgiving Ira.

grounding: A toddler gives back a crayon and pats her cousin after a prompted "sorry", early repair more than understanding.

passage: Daycare note, Thursday. Rekha pulled another child's hair to get the doll. The child cried. I held Rekha's hand and said, "That hurt. She's crying. Can you give the doll back and say sorry?" Rekha looked at the crying child, gave the doll back and stroked the child's hair very gently, where she had pulled. She didn't say sorry. I don't think she understood what she did wrong, but the gentle stroke was a good start. Jagdish, daycare teacher

qa.q: What did Rekha want?
qa.a: The doll.

qa.q: What might Rekha have been feeling when she stroked the child's hair?
qa.a: She may have felt a little worried seeing the child cry and wanted to make it better, even without fully understanding the hurt was her fault.

qa.q: Which choice of Jagdish's worked, and why?
qa.a: Explaining simply and prompting Rekha to give back the doll worked, because it led her to a gentle repair gesture.

qa.q: How might the child whose hair was pulled feel?
qa.a: The child probably felt hurt and upset at first, then a little comforted by the gentle stroke.

grounding: A teacher prompts a toddler to repair after hair-pulling, and she returns the doll and strokes the hair, early reparation.

passage:
In the village courtyard, Ujjwal snatched the neighbour girl's clay whistle and ran. She burst into tears.
His aunt Bidisha caught up with him. “Ujjwal, she's crying. You took her whistle. Say sorry.”
Ujjwal looked at the whistle, then at the girl. He walked back, held it out at arm's length, and when she took it, he flung both arms round her in a clumsy hug.
“Sorry,” Bidisha said for him, softly. The girl sniffed, and blew the whistle.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal snatch from the neighbour girl?
qa.a: He snatched her clay whistle.

qa.q: What does Ujjwal's clumsy hug suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: It suggests he felt some unease at her tears and wanted to make things right; the hug is an early repair, prompted by his aunt, more than an understanding of fault.

qa.q: How did Bidisha help Ujjwal repair things?
qa.a: She named what happened simply, prompted him to give the whistle back, and said "sorry" for him to model the word.

qa.q: How might the neighbour girl feel after getting her whistle back with a hug?
qa.a: She is probably comforted and ready to play again, since she sniffed and blew the whistle.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler giving back a grabbed toy and hugging after an adult prompts sorry, showing early repair more than understanding of fault.
